title: fix: preserve native caller scopes for implicit requirements
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Native Gateway tools derive the minimum scopes required by a method. Treating that generated minimum as an explicit restriction can discard a staff caller's existing broader authority when the method accepts session-only access. Conversely, an explicitly narrowed native request can regain an administrator grant from its surrounding invocation, including when it transfers work to an accepted delayed continuation.

## User Impact

Native tools retain existing broad read, write, or administrator authority for implicit method requirements. Explicit scope arrays, including an empty array, remain exact restrictions. Guest and scoped System callers cannot gain broader permissions from a method minimum or a surrounding invocation.

The restriction also survives nested requests, native autonomous-agent admission, and delayed continuations. An unidentified scoped caller retains its declared read-only or empty vector during a continuation transfer. Explicit transport calls and unmarked plugin dispatch keep their existing contracts; this change adds no public option, protocol field, or persisted state.

## Why This Change Was Made

The native bridge preserves whether scopes were explicitly supplied. The existing dispatcher distinguishes a method minimum from an explicit or retained caller ceiling, qualifies the original admitted authority, and intersects it with the current caller's restriction. A generated session scope retains its broad counterpart only when the source already permits it; explicit restrictions do not regain inherited ADMIN.

Accepted continuations obtain their complete effective ceiling from that same dispatcher. This removes their separate selection of an invocation's original scope vector and preserves the existing rules for source identity, caller narrowing, revocation, and lifetime. Host-owned agent admission still removes human profile attribution without losing the originating permission ceiling. The scope-provenance flag remains internal to the native adapter.

## Evidence

The scope matrix uses the existing registered Gateway fixture and real native request/dispatch functions. It covers staff READ/WRITE/ADMIN, Guest and current caller restrictions, explicit SESSION and empty scopes, scoped or missing-scope System clients, nested requests, and the trusted unbound host route.

- The nested-System regression failed because ADMIN reappeared after an explicit session-only request. Both native agent-launch regressions also failed before their source-ceiling correction.
- The new continuation regression independently reproduced ADMIN reappearing after the same narrowing. The corrected scope and continuation suites passed all 42 cases, including retained source lifetime, disconnected transport, device revocation, and replaced Gateway controls.
- Two scoped-only RPC controls verify that an unidentified empty caller can neither read nor write, while a read-only caller can read but cannot write. Both failed against the incomplete fallback and pass with the final correction.
- The scope file passed all 29 cases with `pnpm test src/gateway/server-plugin-in-process-dispatch.scopes.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` in 28.13 seconds wall time. The retained authorization-file measurement is 32.29 seconds for its original 39-case fixture. Current hosted CI reports 1–7 ms per added scope case (0.038 seconds combined), including 2 ms, 2 ms and 1 ms for the three continuation cases; the two agent-admission cases report 2 ms and 1 ms. Case timings exclude shared setup and transformation. These cases reuse existing fixtures and add no process or server boots.

Fast formatting, lint, conflict and ratchet checks passed on the committed content in 129.71 seconds. Before the necessary conflict rebase, head `2c1ca583261780d87f2ad7f2602a9fec0e0aa9e5` passed all 144 tests in the changed files, typed lint, the production compiler, and all 25 selected test-type graphs remotely. The 13 continuation lifecycle cases remain covered by the qualified 42-case run. Independent source, execution-security and full-PR P2 reviews are clean. [Prior-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35671518108) passed all 129 jobs on its tested merge with main. The completed [ClawSweeper review artifact](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/35672543445) records Platinum for exact head `2c1ca583261780d87f2ad7f2602a9fec0e0aa9e5`, with no findings; its durable public comment is stale.

The [earlier CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35639404857) failed one Bun base64 memory guard: 75,826,753 bytes against its 64 MiB limit, with correct conversion output. An unchanged-baseline run passed all 110 cases, but did not reproduce the original mixed-worker history. The cause remains unresolved; no threshold, runtime or baseline exception has changed. The unchanged Bun case also executed and passed in that subsequent CI run (396 ms). That run qualifies its tested result; the earlier failure remains unexplained and is not claimed repaired. This revision integrates and repairs the newly landed continuation caller.

The final head `83f1a44f38287909ea0ebde69f081164b46781b8` integrates #154991 while preserving its parameter-sensitive scope projection, original caller Stop checks and created-input source guards. The scope calculation moved into a small sibling module to keep the joined dispatcher within the existing line cap. Independent review found both the conflict resolution and extraction clean. On the final tree, the remote scope and continuation suites passed all 49 cases, typed lint and the production compiler passed, and local formatting, lint and all three ratchet checks passed. Earlier full proof is retained for unchanged behavior.
